name: Cefuroxime
route_note: IV/IM as cefuroxime sodium; oral as the prodrug ester cefuroxime axetil (taken with food). Intracameral injection used in cataract surgery.

discovery.note: Developed in the 1970s; its methoxyimino side chain confers stability to many beta-lactamases.

tagline: Second-generation cephalosporin, oral and injectable, used widely for surgical prophylaxis
summary: Cefuroxime is a second-generation cephalosporin developed by Glaxo in the 1970s. It has improved activity against Haemophilus influenzae and Moraxella compared with first-generation agents and is used for respiratory infections, Lyme disease and surgical prophylaxis.
mechanism: Cefuroxime acylates penicillin-binding proteins, blocking peptidoglycan cross-linking.

An alpha-methoxyimino group in its side chain shields the beta-lactam ring from many common beta-lactamases, including those of H. influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis, broadening its Gram-negative spectrum relative to cefalexin.
uses: Community-acquired pneumonia and other lower respiratory tract infections
Intracameral prophylaxis of endophthalmitis after cataract surgery

history.title: First cephalosporins
history.detail: Cefalotin, the first marketed cephalosporin, is launched; later generations extend Gram-negative coverage.

history.title: Launch
history.detail: Glaxo introduces injectable cefuroxime (Zinacef) in the late 1970s.

history.title: Oral prodrug
history.detail: Cefuroxime axetil (Zinnat/Ceftin), an oral ester prodrug, is introduced.

history.title: Intracameral product
history.detail: An intracameral cefuroxime product (Aprokam) is authorised in the EU for cataract surgery prophylaxis.

history.title: WHO AWaRe classification
history.detail: The WHO Essential Medicines List begins grouping antibiotics into Access, Watch and Reserve categories; cefuroxime is placed in the Watch group.

pk.bioavailability: cefuroxime axetil about 37% fasting, about 52% with food
pk.metabolism: axetil ester hydrolysed in gut wall and blood; cefuroxime itself not metabolised

facts: Cefuroxime is classified in the WHO 'Watch' antibiotic group.
